subject: Pilot extension and staged payment / conversion options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Gomez <sara@brightline.com>
Cc: Brightline Procurement <procurement@brightline.com>
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot extension and staged payment / conversion options

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the quick sync today. Per our conversation, we can extend the current time-boxed pilot for another 3 weeks while preserving Brightline's recent performance profile. To keep this lightweight for your finance team, I outlined two clean options below so procurement can choose what maps to your internal cadence.

Option A — Short top-up (fast): 3-week extension, $18,000 flat prepay, includes 100k extra tokens + 1 engineering office hour. No conversion credits.

Option B — Staged top-up (installments + convertibility): 3-week extension split into two installments of $9,500 each (due at amendment signature and 14 days later). If Brightline converts to a 12-month committed package within 60 days after the pilot, we will convert 40% of the total top-up ($7,200) into committed-service credits applied to the first month. This keeps cashflow predictable for you and gives a tangible conversion incentive.

Attachments: I pulled the pilot usage summary (attached) — helps show where credits would land.

Next steps: please let me know which option procurement prefers or what constraints we need to accommodate. If B looks good, I can draft a short amendment and route for e-signature.

Thanks —
Jordan

Jordan, thanks for the clear options — procurement prefers Option B (staged top-up) in principle. A few clarifying questions before we move to an amendment: 

1) Can the second installment be ACH or card? Our AP team generally needs net-30 but we can do 50/50 on signature + net-30 for the second if that simplifies approvals.
2) For conversion credits, can you confirm whether the $7,200 credit would be refundable if we do not convert? (we'd expect not refundable but want to confirm accounting treatment)
3) SLA: our platform team noted that if we scale beyond the pilot thresholds during the extension we may need a short-term SLA uplift for a portion of traffic. Would Redwood agree to an availability target for the extension window as a contractual note?

I've attached our internal procurement checklist and cc'd procurement for visibility. If your team can take these points into account, we can move to a short form amendment.

Best,
Sara

On Fri, May 30, 2025 at 10:03 PM Sara Gomez <sara@brightline.com> wrote:
> Jordan, thanks for the clear options — procurement prefers Option B (staged top-up) in principle. A few clarifying questions before we move to an amendment:
> ...

Sara — thanks, great questions. Quick replies inline below and a proposed amendment approach attached.

1) Payment method / timing: We can accept ACH for the second installment with Net-30 for that second payment (50% on signature, 50% net-30). We will accept card for the initial installment if AP needs faster processing, but note the card processing fee would apply; we can absorb up to $150 of that fee on the first installment for this pilot.

2) Conversion credit treatment: The $7,200 is non-refundable and will only be issued as account credit applied to Redwood usage if Brightline signs a 12-month committed agreement within 60 days. If Brightline does not convert within that window, the credit is forfeited (standard practice). We'll ensure the amendment language calls that out to satisfy audits.

3) SLA uplift: Kimberly, can you confirm we can add a one-line availability target for the 3-week extension window (target: 99.5% system availability for production traffic that touches Redwood inference endpoints) and acceptance criteria? If that's okay, we'll include this as an operational note in the amendment (not a long-term SLA).

Attached: redwood-proposed-amendment-v1.pdf (short form amendment + payment schedule) and the Brightline_Pilot_Usage_Summary.csv (your usage breakout).

If procurement confirms ACH + net-30 for second installment, I'll route the amendment for DocuSign.

Cheers,
Jordan
